title: Uniformly Accelerated Motion
body:
When acceleration is constant, four equations relate the five quantities of
[[Kinematics|motion]]. Each omits one variable, so the choice of equation is decided by asking
which quantity is neither given nor wanted.

```
v = v₀ + at                  omits displacement
Δx = v₀t + ½at²              omits final velocity
v² = v₀² + 2aΔx              omits time
Δx = ½(v₀ + v)t              omits acceleration
```

```
A car at 20 m/s brakes at 5 m/s². How far before it stops?

wanted: Δx     unknown and unwanted: t     so use the third equation
0 = 20² + 2(-5)Δx      ->     Δx = 400/10 = 40 m
```

The equations follow from integrating a constant acceleration twice, which [[CALCULUS 1]]
does directly, and they hold only while the acceleration stays constant. A problem where the
force changes partway through is split into segments, each with its own constant acceleration,
with the final velocity of one becoming the initial velocity of the next.

Free fall is the standard case, with $a = -9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$ for every object regardless of
mass, since the larger gravitational force on a heavier object is exactly offset by its larger
inertia.
